newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks at six-year high on shipping talks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks at six-year high on shipping talks.

text.p: Taiwan share prices rose to a six-year high close on Wednesday on hopes that a Hong Kong meeting of Taiwan and China shipping leaders could yield progress toward ending a ban on direct links, brokers said.

The weighted index finished up 39.73 points or 0.55 percent at 7,290.77. That surpassed the 7,254.32 point close of January 20 which until Wednesday had stood as the highest close since 7,339.71 on June 5, 1990.
Turnover was again hectic at T$114.98 billion.
Shipping shares led the gains, with Yang Ming Marine up 60 cents or 1.6 percent to T$38.1.

Transport officials and shipping executives from Taiwan and China began talks in Hong Kong to discuss direct shipping links between Taiwan's southern Kaohsiung port and southeastern China's Xiamen and Fuzhou ports.
"With shipping shares taking the lead, the celebration rally should last for a couple of days," Albert Lin, an analyst of Golden Securities, said.
First Steamship surged T$1.4 or 6.60 percent to T$22.6.
Market sentiment got an extra boost after Taiwan provincial governor James Soong, who tendered his resignition in December, said he'd return at least temporarily to work, brokers said.
"Soong's returning to work means there will be political stability for the time being, and the market always welcomes that," said Chen Han-chung, analyst for Yungli Securities.
The market was expected to follow its recent rally in the near term, but Golden Securities' Lin noted the market's January bull run had turned speculative, which would limit its life.
"Speculative buying will not last long. The market likely will face heavy selling pressure at around 7,400," Lin said.
A trading range of 7,200-7,400 was seen in the near term, brokers said.
